title: Microphase Continuous Scheduler — KV-locality heuristics and GPU slab slimming for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a 'microphase' variant of the continuous batch scheduler that clusters streaming requests into short, high-cohesion microphases to improve KV cache locality and enable GPU slab slimming for mixed prompt/response length traffic. Target is to reduce peak GPU memory footprint by 8-15% for realistic mixed-turn workloads while preserving P99 latency SLOs. This work blends scheduling heuristics, lightweight request tagging, and a conservative GPU slab compaction signal to safely reclaim fragmented memory without increasing tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic mixed-length workload (70% short prompts, 30% long responses) shows >=8% reduction in peak GPU memory use compared to baseline continuous scheduler
P95 latency change <= +5% and P99 latency <= +10% under target load (95th percentile throughput) compared to baseline
KV cache hit-rate improves or stays within 2% of baseline for production prompt mixes
No observable increase in token-level error or output truncation for evaluated prompt sets
Feature toggle and canary rollouts available; automated rollback if GPU OOMs or P99 increases beyond threshold
design_decisions: Microphase concept: group requests arriving within a short micro-window (~15-40ms) by token-length and KV affinity; prefer co-locating requests that access overlapping KV prefixes to increase hot-token residency

KV-locality heuristic: assign a simple locality_score per stream derived from recent KV key hashes and turn-length buckets (short/medium/long). Locality_score is exponential moving average of overlap between incoming prefix hash and active KV residency map

Slab slimming trigger: conservative watermarks (soft and hard) using free_slab_ratio and fragmentation_index. Soft trigger suggests compaction; hard trigger forces background compaction if fragmentation_index > 0.45 and free_slab_ratio < 0.12
Memory reclamation policy: prefer eviction of cold KV shards and contiguous slab compaction in background; never evict KV entries younger than 1s unless hard OOM risk
Fallback policy: if microphase packing increases observed P99 beyond threshold, scheduler backs off to length-only batching for that GPU for configurable cooldown period
Instrumentation: expose per-GPU microphase_coalesced_percentage, kv_locality_score_p90, slab_fragmentation_index, and compaction_rate metrics
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (spike): prototype microphase windowing in the scheduler simulator and run replay against 3 production traces (chat, assistant, search) — done (branch: spike/microphase-sim)

Phase 2: implement lightweight kv_locality fingerprinting in runtime (adds 8B per stream metadata); change API to carry prefix_hash in streaming frames — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287
Phase 3: integrate slab slimming controller that runs async compaction with rate limiting and safety checks. Compaction runs only when gain_estimate > threshold based on live eviction cost model
Phase 4: add toggle flags (feature gate) and per-shard backoff. Provide admin endpoint to probe slab_fragmentation per GPU
Current branch: feature/microphase-scheduler (WIP). Core scheduler loop changes in scheduler/core/scheduler_microphase.cc. KV fingerprinting patch in runtime/streaming/frame.h
Benchmarks implemented using the benchmark harness (bench/microphase) with 5k qps generated across 32 GPUs to measure compaction safety and latency impact
Safety note: compaction involves small memcpy bursts; throttle default to not exceed 5% of GPU busy time to avoid contention with kernels
test_plan: Unit tests for locality_score computation and micro-window bucketing
Integration test: replay real traffic trace with baseline vs microphase with 95th and 99th latency assertions
Chaos test: randomly trigger compaction during heavy generation to ensure no corruption or increased OOMs
A/B canary test in staging with 10% of traffic on dedicated cluster; collect memory, P95/P99, kv_hit_rate, compaction_events
Long-running soak test (72h) on mixed cluster to detect slow regressions in fragmentation behavior
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge behind feature gate and config defaults (microphase_enabled=false)
Step 1: Internal canary on non-customer dev cluster (10% of dev traffic) for 48h
Step 2: Staging canary with synthetic mixed workloads (20% traffic) for 72h, verify acceptance criteria
Step 3: Production canary on low-risk shard (5% production traffic) for 24h; monitor P99, OOMs, kv_hit_rate and compaction metrics
Step 4: Gradual ramp to 50% over 36h if stable; if any OOM or P99 increase > 10% observed, roll back immediately
Rollback: feature gate off + drain ongoing microphases, then trigger ephemeral slab rebalancer to restore previous slab distribution
